The strict sign sets for upper and lower endpoints are intervals containing zero. On either side the first failed inequality cannot become strict again; the other cannot fail on that side at the same or later index because each width is positive. Thus the proper block and homogeneous tails have exactly the listed pattern, with endpoint ties preserving objective values.

Conversely the weak pattern inequalities give the stated actual clipped length at every index. Each nonempty polyhedron has a nonnegative linear objective on its feasible set; the standard polyhedral attainment result applies even with unbounded feasible slopes.
